Submission Description: (doc-less) Motion to Intervene of Office of the Illinois Attorney General under ER26-3650-000.

ER26-3650-000        Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. submits tariff filing per 35.13(a)(2)(iii): 2026-08-28_Interconnection Reliability Requirements for Large Loads submitted on 8/28/2026 4:41:03 PM, Filing Type code: 10

Filing Party/Contacts:

Filing Party                             Signer (Representative)                  Other Contact (Principal)               
------------                             -----------------------                  -------------------------               
Office of the Illinois Attorney General  samuel.lukens@ilag.gov                   susan.satter@ilag.gov                   

Basis for Intervening:
1. Pursuant to Rule 214 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission”), 18 C.F.R. § 385.214(b), the People of the State of Illinois, by its Attorney General, Kwame Raoul, request to intervene in the above-captioned proceeding. 

2.  Illinois law provides that the Illinois Attorney General "shall have the power and duty on behalf of the people of the State to intervene in, initiate, enforce, and defend all legal proceedings on matters relating to the provision, marketing, and sale of electric . . .  service whenever the Attorney General determines that such action is necessary to promote or protect the rights and interests of all Illinois citizens, classes of customers, and users of electric . . . . services.  15 ILCS 205/6.5(c).  Illinois law also provides that the “Attorney General shall be a party as a matter of right to all proceedings, investigations, and related matters involving the provision of electric, natural gas, water, and telecommunications services before the Illinois Commerce Commission, the courts, and other public bodies." 15 ILCS 205/6.5(d).

3. The People satisfy the requirements of Rule 214 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure that an intervenor have or represent “an interest which may be directly affected by the outcome of the proceeding, including any interest as a . . . consumer.” 18 C.F.R. § 385.214(b). The People represent consumers who will pay the charges for transmission services at MISO.
